analysis.title: Swiss Number Cruncher Temenos - Result
key_insights: Temenos (TEMN) 3Q26 non-IFRS EBIT was USD 109 mn, 10% above consensus (USD 99 mn) and above ZKB-E USD 105 mn, mainly because costs for third-party services and software development fell in absolute terms.

3Q26 subscription and SaaS (licence) revenue was USD 122 mn, +22% YoY in constant currency. That is about 5.4% below consensus (USD 129 mn) and below the +30% guidance, because a major contract in Africa was not secured until 4Q26.
Annual recurring revenue was USD 904 mn, 0.4% above consensus (USD 900 mn). Maintenance revenue grew 7% and was USD 1.3 mn below ZKB's forecast.
Non-IFRS EPS was USD 1.23 vs consensus USD 1.15, an excess of just under 7%, and +32% YoY.
Management raised the FY26 non-IFRS EBIT growth outlook to 12% from 9%, which ZKB estimates implies non-IFRS EBIT of USD 420 mn.
Management raised the FY26 reported EPS growth outlook to 10% from 7%, which ZKB estimates implies EPS of USD 4.62.

Management confirmed FY26 like-for-like constant-currency growth of 9% for subscription and SaaS revenue (implying USD 496 mn) and a 16% like-for-like increase in free cash flow (implying USD 297 mn).
The FY28 guidance was confirmed in full and does not yet include any contribution from additiv AG.

The acquisition of additiv AG, completed 17 July, cost USD 135.3 mn, of which USD 120 mn was settled through additional debt and the remainder through own shares. ZKB considers the price very high because the unit has contributed only minimal revenue or earnings so far.
ZKB values TEMN in FY27 at EV/EBIT of 18.7x and P/E of 22.4x (ZKB-E), close to SAP at EV/EBIT of 19x and P/E of 25x. ZKB reaffirms Market Perform in the absence of price catalysts.

market_movers.rationale: ZKB reaffirms Market Perform on Temenos (CHF 75.10) in the absence of price catalysts. The valuation is close to SAP's, and the additiv acquisition looks expensive.

earnings_insights: Temenos 3Q26 reported: subscription and SaaS revenue USD 122 mn (+22% YoY c.c.) vs consensus USD 129 mn and ZKB-E USD 132 mn. This is below the +30% guidance.
Temenos 3Q26 reported: total revenue USD 293 mn (+13% YoY) vs consensus USD 296 mn and ZKB-E USD 302 mn.
Temenos 3Q26 reported: IFRS EBIT USD 85 mn (+41% YoY, 29% margin) vs ZKB-E USD 83 mn. Non-IFRS EBIT was USD 109 mn (+29% YoY, 37% margin) vs consensus USD 99 mn and ZKB-E USD 105 mn.
Temenos 3Q26 reported: net profit USD 63 mn vs ZKB-E USD 62 mn. Non-IFRS net profit was USD 84 mn, 6.3% above ZKB-E USD 79 mn.

Temenos 3Q26 reported: non-IFRS EPS USD 1.23 vs consensus USD 1.15 and ZKB-E USD 1.18. The non-IFRS adjustments total USD 24.2 mn (restructuring USD 3.0 mn, amortisation USD 11.1 mn, share-based payments USD 10.1 mn) vs ZKB-E USD 22.0 mn.

FY26 guidance (company): non-IFRS EBIT growth of 12% (previously 9%), reported EPS growth of 10% (previously 7%), subscription and SaaS growth of 9% like-for-like c.c., free cash flow growth of 16% like-for-like. The FY26 SaaS guidance includes a marginal contribution from additiv.
ZKB FY26E EPS is USD 4.08 and FY27E EPS is USD 4.80 (FY25 USD 3.31). ZKB's implied FY26 reported EPS from management guidance is USD 4.62.
risk_factors: Large contracts can slip between quarters, as a major Africa contract did into 4Q26. This leaves subscription and SaaS revenue below guidance in 3Q26.
The additiv AG acquisition was funded with USD 120 mn of additional debt and has so far contributed minimal revenue or earnings. FY28 guidance does not yet include it.
The 3Q26 earnings beat came mainly from lower absolute costs for third-party services and software development, not from revenue.

tension_points.bull_case: Non-IFRS EBIT beat consensus by 10% and non-IFRS EPS by just under 7% on lower absolute costs. FY26 earnings guidance was raised, with non-IFRS EBIT growth to 12% from 9% and EPS growth to 10% from 7%.
tension_points.bear_case: Subscription and SaaS revenue of USD 122 mn missed consensus by 5.4% and the +30% guidance after a major Africa contract slipped to 4Q26. The additiv acquisition cost USD 135.3 mn with minimal contribution so far.

theme_stances.key_argument: Earnings beat on cost management, subscription and SaaS revenue disappointed, and the additiv acquisition looks expensive, so ZKB sees no price catalyst.
theme_stances.evidence: We reaffirm our “Market Perform” rating in the absence of price catalysts.
